test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 27 Feb 2021 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following is NOT an Indian research base at Antarctica?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Dakshin Yamunotri**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Dakshin Yamunotri** is not an Indian research base in Antarctica.
 
• India has set up three research stations in Antarctica: **Dakshin Gangotri**, **Maitri**, and **Bharati**.
 
• **Dakshin Gangotri** was the first Indian scientific research base station in Antarctica, established in 1983-84.
 
• **Maitri** was commissioned in 1989 and is India's second research station in Antarctica.
 
• **Bharati** is the third research base and was established in 2012.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dakshin Gangotri**

 
 
• It was the first Indian scientific research base station in Antarctica.
 
• Established during the third Indian expedition to Antarctica in 1983-84.
 
• Currently, it is used as a supply base and transit camp.
 
 
 
• **Maitri**
 
 
• Commissioned in 1989, it is India's second research station in Antarctica.
 
• It is located on the rocky mountainous region called Schirmacher Oasis.
 
• Maitri has living accommodation for 25 people and is used for various research activities.
 
 
 
• **Bharati**
 
 
• Established in 2012, Bharati is India's third research base in Antarctica.
 
• It is located in the Larsemann Hills.
 
• The station is a modern, eco-friendly facility and can accommodate 47 people in the main building.
 
• Bharati supports research in atmospheric, biological, earth, and marine sciences.
